description: The DS-1000 cross-system performance set: every datasets/ds1000/ds1000_case<NNNN> folder with one status. Written by tools/perf_case_set.py; edit the decisions in tools/ds1000_perf.py and tools/perf_fixtures.py, not this file.

rules.status_order: RQ1_ACCEPTED in tools/ds1000_perf.py takes precedence: every accepted program is perf. Other programs retain their historical status (including the eight legacy perf cases rejected in RQ1). Former exclusion rules below are historical, not new filters.
rules.out_of_scope: The DS-1000 program is out of scope in ds1000_numpy/manifest.json: it imports or uses a module other than numpy (incl. submodules) and math (the author's rule), or another rule of datasets/FILTERING.md fires (non-numeric data, NaN/infinity, ...), checked on the solution text and on every DS-1000 test input.
rules.degenerate: No output depends on a private input: every output is fixed by the parameter types and the constants, so there is nothing to prove.
rules.duplicate: The kernel computes the same function as a case with a lower id; the lower id is kept. Three tests: the kernels are identical after renaming local variables (same types and constants); or, fed the same input values, the outputs are a fixed reordering or reshaping of the other case's (numeric test on both cases' fixtures); or both only copy input cells to outputs (no arithmetic or comparison) and copy the same number of cells the same number of times with the same constant outputs, so they are the same circuit up to which cells are read (input cells no output reads are ignored: no system needs to load them).
rules.zinnia_rejects: Zinnia at the commit in `zinnia_probe` refuses the kernel: compilation fails, or it compiles but Zinnia refuses to build a witness for either fixture input, or neither the halo2-base nor the Noir backend synthesizes the circuit (error recorded). Provisional: compiler fixes on other branches may change it. A case only one backend refuses stays perf and is listed under zinnia_backend_gaps.
rules.perf: Every program in tools/ds1000_perf.py RQ1_ACCEPTED, plus the eight retained legacy perf cases. Duplicates and constant-output programs are included; former_status and former_duplicate_of preserve the original classification. Analysis filters legacy perf programs rejected in RQ1.
rules.kernels: Every in-scope kernel is the output of tools/generate_ds1000_kernels.py (shapes from the record's last DS-1000 test case; each dtype the narrowest of Boolean < Integer < Float < Complex holding the parameter in every test case; returns the value DS-1000 checks) with the shape parameters listed in tools/ds1000_perf.py bound as compile-time constants and the existing 0318/0319 permutation preconditions documented in FILTERING.md. tools/perf_case_set.py --check verifies it.
rules.shape_constants: Author decision 2026-10-06: in the performance set, DS-1000 shape parameters (values that fix an array shape or a trip count) are compile-time constants with their DS-1000 test-case value. The runtime variants are in the acceptance set (ds1000_numpy/generated/).
rules.data_movement_only: true when the outputs depend on private inputs only by copying them (no arithmetic or comparison on private values). Such cases stay `perf` but can be reported separately.
rules.numbers: Every system computes floats in Q32 fixed point (BRIEF.md). Zinnia's quantizer (src/prove/field.rs `quantize`) rounds v * 2^32 to the nearest integer; BRIEF.md says trunc. Integer parameters are 64-bit integers.
rules.float_tolerance: The output check compares each float output with NumPy on input B as |actual - expected| <= atol + rtol * |expected|. Outputs that copy an input get atol = 2^-32 (one Q32 step), rtol = 0. Computed outputs get atol = rtol = 1e-6: Q32 resolves 2.3e-10 and these kernels round at most a few thousand times on values below 10^7, so an implementation of the same computation lands well inside, while a precision loss to ~16 fractional bits or a wrong value does not. Integer and boolean outputs are compared exactly (`float_tolerance` is null).

selection.how: author selection update; NumPy fixture validation only; no new Zinnia probes
selection.historical_evidence: zinnia_probe and per-case zinnia fields are retained historical observations, not validation of the present compiler or the new selection

zinnia_probe.compiler_sources: unchanged since e58e9a6 (src/, zinnia/ as of the eval-redo snapshot); git diff e58e9a6 -- src zinnia is empty

zinnia_probe.how: tools/zinnia_probe.py: ZKCircuit.from_method(kernel).compile() in a child process, 300 s limit, 8 GB memory cap; fixtures mock-proved with backend='mock'

zinnia_backend_gaps.meaning: perf cases whose circuit one Zinnia backend cannot synthesize (emit_structural on input B)

zinnia_output_mismatches.meaning: perf cases where Zinnia's mock prover accepts the honest witness but its public outputs do not match NumPy on a fixture input: Zinnia computes a different function (compiler bug)
